caption: Kansas v. Glover
subject: Officer has reasonable suspicion to stop a vehicle on learning the registered owner has a revoked license, absent info negating inference owner is driving

caption: Hernandez v. Mesa
subject: No Bivens damages remedy for cross-border shooting by U.S. Border Patrol agent

caption: Taylor v. Riojas
subject: Qualified immunity denied where any reasonable officer would know confining inmate in shockingly unsanitary cells is unconstitutional (obviousness)

caption: Tanzin v. Tanvir
subject: RFRA authorizes money damages against federal officers (FBI agents) in their individual capacities; No Fly List retaliation

caption: Brownback v. King
subject: FTCA judgment bar; whether dismissal of FTCA claim bars companion Bivens claims from same federal task-force encounter

caption: McCoy v. Alamu
subject: Qualified immunity GVR'd in light of Taylor v. Riojas; corrections officer pepper-sprayed inmate without provocation

caption: Uzuegbunam v. Preczewski
subject: Nominal damages alone redress a completed constitutional violation, preserving live Sec.1983 case (campus speech)

caption: Torres v. Madrid
subject: Application of physical force to the body with intent to restrain is a Fourth Amendment seizure even if the person is not subdued and escapes

caption: Caniglia v. Strom
subject: No freestanding community-caretaking exception authorizing warrantless entry into and seizure inside a home (welfare check, firearms)

caption: United States v. Cooley
subject: Tribal police officer has authority to temporarily detain and search a non-Indian on a public right-of-way through a reservation

caption: Lange v. California
subject: Pursuit of a fleeing misdemeanant does not categorically justify warrantless entry into a home; exigency assessed case-by-case

caption: Lombardo v. City of St. Louis
subject: Excessive-force prone-restraint of detainee requires careful, context-specific totality analysis; vacated grant to officers

caption: Rivas-Villegas v. Cortesluna
subject: Officer entitled to qualified immunity on excessive-force claim (knee to back briefly while disarming suspect); no clearly established law

caption: City of Tahlequah v. Bond
subject: Officers entitled to qualified immunity in fatal shooting; no precedent clearly establishing the conduct violated the Fourth Amendment

caption: Hemphill v. New York
subject: Sixth Amendment Confrontation; opening-the-door theory does not justify admitting an absent witness's plea allocution

caption: Federal Bureau of Investigation v. Fazaga
subject: FISA Sec.1806(f) does not displace the state-secrets privilege; suit over alleged FBI surveillance of Muslim community

caption: Thompson v. Clark
subject: Sec.1983 Fourth Amendment malicious-prosecution claim requires only that the criminal proceeding ended without a conviction

caption: Egbert v. Boule
subject: No Bivens remedy for Fourth Amendment excessive-force or First Amendment retaliation claims against a Border Patrol agent

caption: Vega v. Tekoh
subject: A violation of Miranda's prophylactic rules is not a deprivation of a right that supports a Sec.1983 claim

caption: Nance v. Ward
subject: Sec.1983 is the proper vehicle for a method-of-execution claim even where the requested relief would require a change in state law

caption: Reed v. Goertz
subject: Statute of limitations for a Sec.1983 procedural-due-process claim seeking DNA testing accrues when state postconviction litigation ends

caption: Dupree v. Younger
subject: Purely legal issue resolved at summary judgment is preserved for appeal without a post-trial Rule 50 motion; arose from Sec.1983 excessive-force suit vs corrections lieutenant

caption: Health and Hospital Corp. of Marion County v. Talevski
subject: Spending-Clause (FNHRA nursing-home) rights are presumptively enforceable through Sec.1983

caption: Samia v. United States
subject: Confrontation Clause not violated by admitting a non-testifying codefendant's confession altered to avoid naming defendant, with limiting instruction

caption: Federal Bureau of Investigation v. Fikre
subject: Government's removal of plaintiff from No Fly List did not moot his suit against FBI agents under voluntary-cessation doctrine

caption: Culley v. Marshall
subject: Due Process requires only a timely forfeiture hearing, not a separate preliminary hearing, after seizure of a car in civil forfeiture

caption: National Rifle Association of America v. Vullo
subject: Sec.1983 First Amendment claim that state financial regulator unconstitutionally coerced regulated firms to disassociate from advocacy group

caption: Chiaverini v. City of Napoleon
subject: Sec.1983 Fourth Amendment malicious-prosecution claim can proceed on a charge lacking probable cause even if another charge was supported

caption: Gonzalez v. Trevino
subject: Sec.1983 First Amendment retaliatory-arrest claim; Nieves probable-cause exception not limited to comparator evidence of same conduct

caption: Smith v. Arizona
subject: Confrontation Clause; substitute forensic analyst conveying an absent analyst's testimonial statements for their truth implicates confrontation

caption: Williams v. Reed
subject: State exhaustion requirement that bars state courts from hearing delay-based claims is preempted by Sec.1983

caption: Lackey v. Stinnie
subject: Plaintiff who obtains only a preliminary injunction is not a prevailing party entitled to Sec.1988 attorney's fees

caption: Barnes v. Felix
subject: Fourth Amendment excessive-force analysis uses totality of the circumstances; rejects the moment-of-threat rule (traffic-stop shooting)

caption: Martin v. United States
subject: FTCA; Supremacy Clause does not bar liability and law-enforcement proviso analysis for FBI SWAT raid on wrong house

caption: Perttu v. Richards
subject: Seventh Amendment jury trial on PLRA exhaustion where exhaustion is intertwined with merits; underlying Sec.1983 prisoner claims vs officer

caption: Gutierrez v. Saenz
subject: Death-row prisoner has Article III standing to bring Sec.1983 due-process challenge to state postconviction DNA-testing procedures

caption: Medina v. Planned Parenthood South Atlantic
subject: Medicaid any-qualified-provider provision does not confer an individual right enforceable through Sec.1983

caption: Goldey v. Fields
subject: No Bivens cause of action for Eighth Amendment excessive-force claim by prisoner against federal Bureau of Prisons officers

caption: Case v. Montana
subject: Fourth Amendment emergency-aid; warrantless home entry to render aid needs objectively reasonable basis to believe emergency exists, not probable cause

caption: Postal Service v. Konan
subject: FTCA postal-matter exception bars claims for intentional non-delivery or misdelivery of mail by USPS employees

caption: The GEO Group, Inc. v. Menocal
subject: Collateral-order doctrine does not permit federal contractor to immediately appeal denial of derivative sovereign (Yearsley) immunity

caption: Villarreal v. Texas
subject: Sixth Amendment; qualified order barring discussion of defendant's own testimony during overnight recess does not violate right to counsel

caption: Olivier v. City of Brandon
subject: Heck v. Humphrey does not bar a Sec.1983 suit seeking purely prospective relief by a plaintiff previously convicted under the challenged law

caption: Zorn v. Linton
subject: Officer entitled to qualified immunity for a routine wristlock on a protester after a verbal warning; no clearly established law

caption: District of Columbia v. R.W.
subject: Fourth Amendment reasonable suspicion for a stop is judged on the totality of circumstances (unprovoked flight); courts cannot excise individual facts

caption: Hencely v. Fluor Corp.
subject: Boyle federal-contractor defense is narrow; state tort claims not preempted where Government did not direct the challenged conduct (base bombing)

caption: Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety
subject: RLUIPA (Spending Clause) does not permit individual-capacity money-damages liability against prison officials absent knowing consent

caption: Chatrie v. United States
subject: Obtaining cell-phone location data via a geofence warrant is a Fourth Amendment search; individual has a legitimate expectation of privacy in that data
